qs.q: A 50-year-old presents with heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, generalized oedema, and hyperlipidaemia. Which of the following clinical syndromes best matches this constellation of findings?
qs.e: The defining manifestations of nephrotic syndrome include proteinuria greater than 3.5 g/day, hypoalbuminemia, oedema, hyperlipidaemia, and lipiduria. Nephritic syndrome is classically characterized by haematuria, red cell casts, and hypertension.
qs.s: Glomerular Diseases: Classification, Histology & Pathology: MCQs

qs.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with heavy proteinuria exceeding 4.0 g/day, marked pitting peripheral oedema, hypoalbuminaemia, and severe hyperlipidaemia. Which urinary finding is most characteristic of her underlying condition?
o: Fatty casts and oval fat bodies in urine
Leucocyte and granular casts in samples
Red blood cell casts and oval fat bodies
Waxy and broad renal casts in sediment
qs.e: Nephrotic syndrome is characterized by heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminaemia, and hyperlipidaemia, often shedding fatty casts and oval fat bodies in the urine. Red blood cell casts are instead a hallmark of nephritic syndrome.
qs.s: Renal, Liver, Cardiac & Adrenal Function Tests: MCQs
